Class EMFInstancePopulator

java.lang.Object
io.github.lorenzobettini.emfmodelgenerator.EMFInstancePopulator
public class EMFInstancePopulator extends Object
Populates existing EMF EObjects with sample data. This includes setting attribute values and populating both containment and cross references, with support for configurable multi-valued counts and maximum depth for recursive population. It also handles feature maps, which allow heterogeneous collections.

This class performs only the population step: callers create the root objects and, when required, put them in resources and save those resources themselves. For example, an object whose metamodel has already been loaded can be populated directly:

EClass libraryClass = (EClass) ePackage.getEClassifier("Library");
EObject library = EcoreUtil.create(libraryClass);

EMFInstancePopulator populator = new EMFInstancePopulator();
populator.populateEObjects(library);

Population can be tailored globally and for individual structural features. Per-feature functions are useful when deterministic domain-shaped sample values are needed:

EAttribute name = (EAttribute) libraryClass.getEStructuralFeature("name");
EReference books = (EReference) libraryClass.getEStructuralFeature("books");

EMFInstancePopulator populator = new EMFInstancePopulator();
populator.functionForAttribute(name,
    owner -> "Sample " + owner.eClass().getName());
populator.setContainmentReferenceMaxCountFor(books, 3);
populator.setMaxDepth(2);
populator.populateEObjects(library);

When roots may refer to one another, attach them to resources in the same resource set and pass them to one populateEObjects(EObject...) call. This lets cross-reference selection see the complete population before references are assigned.

Author:
Lorenzo Bettini

    • functionForAttribute

      public void functionForAttribute(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EAttribute attribute, EMFAttributeSetter.EMFAttributeValueFunction function)
      Set a custom function for generating values for the given EAttribute. For example, a name can be derived from the owning object's class: 
      populator.functionForAttribute(nameAttribute,
    owner -> "Sample " + owner.eClass().getName());
      Parameters:
      attribute - the EAttribute for which to set the function
      function - the function to generate values for the attribute

    • functionForCrossReference

      public void functionForCrossReference(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EReference reference, EMFCrossReferenceSetter.EMFCrossReferenceValueFunction function)
      Set a custom function for generating values for the given cross EReference. Returning null delegates that invocation to the default candidate selection: 
      populator.functionForCrossReference(authorReference, book -> {
    EObject preferredAuthor = findPreferredAuthor(book);
    return preferredAuthor; // null means: use the default candidate
});
      Parameters:
      reference - the cross EReference for which to set the function
      function - the function to generate values for the cross reference

    • setMaxDepth

      public void setMaxDepth(int maxDepth)
      Set the maximum recursion depth for populating containment references. Attributes are always populated regardless of depth. A root is at depth 0; with a maximum depth of 1, its direct contained objects are created and have their attributes populated, but their containment references are not expanded.
      Parameters:
      maxDepth - the maximum depth

    • populateEObjects

      public void populateEObjects(org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EObject... rootInstances)
      Populate the given EObjects with sample data. This includes setting attribute values and populating both containment and cross references, up to the configured maximum depth.

      All roots are populated before cross-references are assigned. Supply related roots together so that each one can be selected as a cross-reference candidate for the others:

      EObject book = EcoreUtil.create(bookClass);
EObject author = EcoreUtil.create(authorClass);
bookResource.getContents().add(book);
authorResource.getContents().add(author);

EMFInstancePopulator populator = new EMFInstancePopulator();
populator.populateEObjects(book, author);
      The resources in this example must belong to the same ResourceSet. Objects created through containment during the call are recursively populated as well.
      Parameters:
      rootInstances - the EObjects to populate
